correctness.rationale: The integral Binet identity follows from the split characteristic roots. Because a is primitive modulo p^r for p>=5, a+1 is a unit and the least period is T=phi(p^r), as J_s=0 and J_(s+1)=1 force s even and a^s=1. Even indices enumerate square units exactly once, odd indices nonsquare units exactly once; the Legendre indicators therefore count exactly one hit per qualifying branch. Their overlap is c_p, computed by standard quadratic-character sums including sum_z chi(z^2-1)=-1, proved via the bijection (u-v)(u+v)=1. Inclusion-exclusion and total hits give H0,H1,H2. All boundary cases p>=5,r>=1 are included, and zero/one/two is an infinite theorem, not inferred from finite tests. The standalone program independently verified 76 primitive-root parameter cases, 583944 targets, and 566784 terms.

originality.rationale: The claim is not a mere Binet formula or non-surjectivity assertion: it determines every target multiplicity, every prime-power histogram, the sharp least period, and the parameter-independent mod-eight bias. Full-text comparisons show older authors establish the recurrence, while the closest 2026 complete-modulus result concerns which moduli are fully represented, not the fine fibers in the primitive-root regime. Searches have not identified a theorem logically implying all these conclusions; equivalence in uncatalogued Lucas-fiber literature remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed general results on quadratic-character coset intersections or Lucas sequence modular fiber distributions might imply this special case.
No exhaustive worldwide survey of books, dissertations, inaccessible print papers or all later citations was performed.
The same recurrence and Binet formula were previously published, so only the fine primitive-root fiber profile is proposed as new.

value.rationale: Modular output statistics are a natural refinement of the published question of whether Jacobsthal recurrence residues are complete. Exact singular/overlap fiber frequencies in all prime-power residue rings are a nontrivial, well-motivated invariant even where the image is known to be proper. The result identifies every attainable target and its multiplicity, the minimal period, sharp maximum two, a uniform lift law, and an explicit mod-eight histogram independent of the primitive-root parameter, answering a natural complete classification problem; no downstream theorem or Artin-style infinitude is asserted.
